summary: AE/SE walkthrough of Redwood SDKs (Python & TS), auth patterns (API key, SSO/SAML, service accounts), and environment setup for a pilot. Discussed hosted vs Dedicated, VPC/private plane concerns, and basic Optimize suggestions for batching. Action items assigned for sandbox access and a perf run.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-29 14:00 PST | Duration: ~52 min | Recorder: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Riley Gomez (Redwood SE), Ankit Rao (Redwood DevAdv), Oliver Hayes (SignalPath), Priya Nand (SignalPath), Marcus Li (SignalPath CTO - joined 00:22), Dana (Product PM)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a rainy tuesday, appreciate you blocking. i'm maya from redwood, riley is our se, ankit will jump in on a couple of code bits. quick yes/no go around?
[00:07] Oliver: yep oliver here, we'll mostly be hands-on, priya and dana too.
[00:11] Priya: yep thanks, curious about auth and ci secrets flow mostly.
[00:15] Riley: cool; agenda is quick intro, pip/npm install, auth patterns (api key, service account/saml, k8s secrets), demo of console for env vars, then a short walkthrough of optimize and batching suggestions. save q's for the end or drop in chat.

[00:55] Ankit: small note before we start - our SDKs are identical surface for python and ts. should i open a small scratch repo?
[01:02] Oliver: please do, we have a repo template we can paste into.

[01:48] Riley: ok i'll share my screen -- starting with python: pip install redwood-sdk (transcriber: package name may be 'redwood' or 'redwood-client' depending on the pip index) then set REDWOOD_API_KEY as env var. we walked through an example: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']); resp = client.text.generate("summarize: ...").
[01:55] Oliver: question - can we store keys in vault and have CI pick them up?
[02:10] Priya: we use vault + GitHub actions secrets.
[02:18] Maya: yep supported. recommended pattern is store key in your secret manager, inject into CI as REDWOOD_API_KEY, then ephemeral service account keys for long-running workloads. for private deployments we support service accounts + role based tokens.

[03:05] Priya: what about sso / scim? we need scim provisioning for users.
[03:18] Riley: we have SSO / SAML + SCIM available on enterprise plans. can map groups to RBAC roles in console. we'll attach the auth docs after.

[04:12] Ankit: switching to typescript quick snippet -- npm i @redwoodai/sdk (note: name slurred in transcript), import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwoodai/sdk'; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const out = await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] });
[04:40] Oliver: does the ts client stream natively?
[04:46] Riley: yes — streaming via event emitter or async iterator depending on runtime. the node SDK supports server-sent events pattern and the browser uses fetch streams. small caveat: in serverless you may want to use our SDK's reconnect helpers to avoid cold start token refetch.

[05:30] Priya: can you demo the console where we set envs per-route?
[05:36] Riley: sure - opening console -- (screen noise) under Projects > Environments you can add variables scoped to route or model. we showed the variable UI, ability to mark secrets, and attach to canary rollouts. there was a small pause while he navigated.
[06:55] Riley: note: you can also link a KMS (aws-kms or gcp-kms) so secrets are envelope-encrypted. we recommend KMS for Dedicated/Private.

[07:40] Oliver: on Dedicated vs hosted: our data is sensitive, policy team leans private, but cost team is worried. what's the common compromise?
[07:52] Maya: lots of customers start hosted to move fast, then Dedicated (reserved pools) or Private (VPC + control plane) when they hit compliance. for SignalPath, we suggested pilot on hosted with VPC-peering or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) if you need key separation, then upgrade.
[08:25] Marcus (joined): hi all, sorry running late, want to hear the auth & perf bits, timeline is Q1 pilot ideally.
[08:40] Maya: great, quick note on timelines - sandbox access we can do within day, pilot sizing usually 2-4 weeks for a basic perf run.

[09:10] Riley: moving to Optimize — we looked at two levers: batching and prefix/KV caching. for your ingestion pipeline (long-document summarization) we recommended 1) enable continuous batching on the model route, 2) precompute embeddings for repeated doc seeds, and 3) use quantized model variant for non-sensitive text to save cost.
[09:45] Oliver: how much latency impact with batching?
[09:51] Riley: depends on arrival distribution; we've seen p95 go up a little but p50 improves and unit cost drops ~30% in many cases. we can tune max batch latency to meet your SLO.

[11:05] Priya: security—what about audit logs and retention?
[11:12] Riley: audit logs (API + console ops) are available with enterprise packages, and you can export to your SIEM. retention configurable, and logs include token-level cost for chargeback. we'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs.

[12:00] Ankit: quick live-code: we'll push a tiny GH action workflow snippet that reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from secrets and runs a test that hits the sandbox. (noise) snippet printed: name: smoke; steps: uses: actions/checkout; run: python -m pytest tests/test_smoke.py; env: REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}.
[12:38] Oliver: does redwood support ephemeral creds for CI workers?
[12:44] Riley: yes, service accounts with short-lived tokens; rotating keys built into the console, or you can integrate OIDC for GitHub to mint tokens.

[14:20] Maya: let's do a short demo of a perf test. Riley, can you kick off the sample run?
[14:28] Riley: starting load script - note: in sandbox this will be limited. we run 100 concurrent tasks, each summarizing a 2k token doc. p50 roughly 120ms per token in dedicated envs, but sandbox will be slower.
[15:10] (sound of typing)
[16:05] Riley: initial stream: several timeouts in sandbox, but important for us to do your perf on your network path. i'll provide a perf-run checklist: egress path, region pin, model variant, batch params.
[16:33] Oliver: can we run inside our VPC? we prefer no traffic leaving.
[16:40] Riley: for Private you can run fully on-prem or VPC-peered with private control plane; for Dedicated there's a customer-dedicated subnet option. both support BYOK via KMS/HSM.

[18:01] Priya: curious about model pinning and rollbacks — we'd want predictable outputs.
[18:08] Riley: console supports pinning model versions per-route and automatic fallback to compatible variants if a rollout fails. we demoed a simple canary with 10% traffic.

[19:12] Dana: on costs — can you give a quick sense, even ballpark?
[19:20] Maya: quick ballpark: hosted gen cost ~ $0.?. (transcriber unclear) let's follow up with a tailored estimate once we have sample qps and token characteristics. for dedicated we gave an example monthly commit for a 4x A100 equivalent pool; we'll include numbers in the follow-up.

[22:05] Ankit: small dev note: when using streaming in node, watch for backpressure; our sdk exposes chunk size and a reconnect handler. also typenames across py/ts slightly differ - we'll add a minimal compatibility table.

[24:30] Oliver: someone on legal will ask about data residency - europe user data we need it to stay within eu.
[24:38] Riley: we have region pinning and can provision private plane in eu-west-1; retention + residency are configurable.

[26:45] Maya: quick walk-through of the sandbox invite I sent — it's a limited org with pre-provisioned routes and sample keys. you can rotate keys in console and enable the sandbox KMS tie-in.

[28:00] Oliver: during pilot do you help run a benchmark?
[28:08] Maya: yes SE-assisted perf run is standard. riley will own the run, share the script, and we'll help interpret traces.

[30:23] (short silence, typing)
[31:05] Marcus: one high level ask — we need to make sure any PII is scrubbed before it leaves our environment; what are the options?
[31:14] Riley: options: 1) client-side filtering & redaction (we recommend), 2) field-level masking + only send embeddings for sensitive fields, 3) Private deployment which never egresses data off your network. also we support tokenization hooks in the SDK to do local processing before send.

[33:09] Priya: can we have a short checklist of all the docs to share?
[33:16] Maya: yes - we'll send: SSO/SCIM guide, RBAC mapping, KMS/BYOK integration doc, perf-run checklist, CI/GH Actions example, and SOC2 + ISO attestation.

[34:32] Ankit: small tangent on retries — SDK default backoff is exponential with jitter; if you're doing high-volume batch jobs we recommend explicit idempotency keys.

[36:00] Oliver: ok last technical q: can we run model fine-tunes or will we rely on prompts?
[36:05] Riley: currently we support prompt-based tuning and embeddings + retrieval; hosted fine-tuning roadmaps vary by vendor model licensing. for many customers retrieval-augmented generation + prompt engineering hits the bar. we'll map your cases in the follow-up.

[38:22] Dana: what do you need from us to start the pilot?
[38:29] Maya: three things: 1) sample prompt set + SLOs, 2) expected qps and token distribution, 3) decision on whether pilot uses hosted sandbox or private/dedicated path.

[39:10] Oliver: we'll prepare that.

[40:02] Riley: quick demo wrap - showed console route config, env secrets, model pinning, canary rollout and a short optimize panel with batching slider.

[41:15] Marcus: ok i'm sold on trying hosted sandbox first but with BYOK and region pin; we'll escalate if policy blocks.

[42:00] Maya: recap / next steps — provision sandbox, share security docs, schedule a perf check-in. do we have consensus on owners?
[42:12] Oliver: yes, oliver will own the prompt set and perf targets, priya will own infra and region/residency constraints.

[42:35] Maya: perfect. we'll email credentials and the docs. riley you'll take perf-run lead?
[42:40] Riley: yup I'll own that.

[43:05] (small crosstalk)
[44:00] Maya: any other q's?
[44:05] Priya: just one - does the sandbox support webhook event delivery for async jobs?
[44:12] Riley: yes, webhooks for job completion and streaming callbacks are supported; you can configure endpoint retries and sig validation.

[45:20] Ankit: i'll add a minimal sample repo to the invite thread after the call.

[46:10] Maya: great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items.
[46:20] Oliver: thanks, good session.
[46:35] (meeting ends, some participants lingered in chat)

Notes: transcript has imperfect product names and package names. references to shared artifacts: "sandbox invite" (link sent in calendar), perf-run checklist (will be attached in follow-up), security whitepaper (SOC2/ISO).
